name: Shecaniah
title: The Levite Who Led the People's Repentance
summary: Shecaniah is a biblical figure who appears in connection with the return from exile in Babylon. He is best known for his role in the people's repentance and covenant renewal under Ezra and Nehemiah, where he confessed the people's sin regarding mixed marriages and urged action. The name Shecaniah is borne by several individuals in the Old Testament, but the most prominent one is the man who took the initiative to make a covenant to send away foreign wives.

keyEvents.title: Confession of Sin Regarding Mixed Marriages
keyEvents.description: Shecaniah, son of Jehiel, from the descendants of Elam, spoke up and confessed to Ezra that the people had been unfaithful to God by taking foreign wives from the peoples of the land.

keyEvents.title: Call to Make a Covenant with God
keyEvents.description: Shecaniah proposed that the people make a covenant with God to send away all the foreign wives and their children, in accordance with the law.

keyEvents.title: Encouragement for Ezra to Act
keyEvents.description: Shecaniah encouraged Ezra to step forward and lead the work of addressing the mixed marriages, assuring him that the people would support him.

keyEvents.title: Ezra's Grief and the Gathering of the People
keyEvents.description: Following Shecaniah's initiative, Ezra gathered the people in Jerusalem, where all the men from Judah and Benjamin came together to take a stand on the matter of foreign wives.

keyEvents.title: Implementation of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: As a result of Shecaniah's initiative, a systematic review of all mixed marriages was launched, and those who had taken foreign wives committed to sending them away.

keyEvents.title: Shecaniah Mentioned in the Book of Nehemiah
keyEvents.description: A Shecaniah, son of Arah, is also mentioned in connection with Nehemiah's work and the rebuilding of Jerusalem, showing the family's involvement in the restoration.
